text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince Hassan says King Hussein's meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday will have strategic importance.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali says U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright's statement on Iraq was interference in its domestic affairs.
- Cabinet says Egyptian workers in Jordan have until April 31 to get their permits in order.
- Hamas former politburo chief Moussa Abu Marzouq says United States still trying to move him to Jordan or Egypt.

- Sources say government studies cutting bread prices to 150 fils (21 cents) a kilo after recent falls in wheat prices and restricting cash assistance to those receiving support from national assistance fund.
- Majali: "We're wholeheartedly with the Iraqi people."
- Crown Prince Hassan says differences of opinion should only occur in the context of legality, unity and national interests.
- Senior planning ministry source says World Bank's International Finance Corporation studying funding of small projects in Jordan.
- Crown Prince reviews issues facing Jordan and the Middle East, approach to peace and development.
- Majali says Albright comments could boost support for Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.
- Islamists stand out in demands for changes in electoral system.
